## Common Electrical Problems in Fort Lauderdale Homes

Fort Lauderdale’s aging housing stock and South Florida’s climate create specific electrical hazards. These require a licensed Fort Lauderdale electrician.

### 🔴 [Circuit Breakers Tripping Repeatedly](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/breaker-keeps-tripping-fort-lauderdale/)

A circuit breaker that trips more than once is a warning sign of an overloaded circuit, a short circuit, or a failing breaker. Call Fort Lauderdale Electricians immediately rather than continuing to reset the breaker. Left unaddressed, a repeatedly tripping breaker can cause overheating and electrical fires.

### 🔴 [Flickering or Dimming Lights](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/flickering-lights-fort-lauderdale/)

Lights that flicker throughout your Fort Lauderdale home indicate loose wiring connections, a failing breaker, or a service entrance problem. Intermittent flickering is often caused by loose neutral connections that create dangerous arcing inside your walls. This is a fire hazard requiring immediate diagnosis.

### 🔴 [Burning Smell from Outlets or Panel](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/burning-smell-outlet-fort-lauderdale/)

A burning smell from an outlet, switch, or electrical panel is an emergency. Shut off the circuit immediately and call Fort Lauderdale Electricians at 954-477-8240. Burning electrical smells indicate arcing, overheating insulation, or a failing connection — all can ignite a house fire within minutes.

### 🟡 [Outdated Electrical Panel](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/electrical-panel-upgrade-fort-lauderdale/)

Many Fort Lauderdale homes have panels now known to be fire hazards. [Federal Pacific Stab-Lok panels](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/federal-pacific-panel-replacement-fort-lauderdale/) and [Zinsco panels](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/zinsco-panel-replacement-fort-lauderdale/) are two of the most common dangerous panels in Fort Lauderdale’s housing stock. Free panel inspections and 200A service upgrades throughout Broward County.

### 🟡 [Aluminum Wiring (1965–1975 Homes)](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/aluminum-wiring-fort-lauderdale/)

Fort Lauderdale homes built between 1965 and 1975 frequently contain aluminum branch circuit wiring. Aluminum expands and contracts more than copper, causing connections to loosen over time — creating resistance heat that can start fires inside walls without visible warning signs.

### 🟡 [Partial Power Loss](https://www.fortlauderdaleelectricians.net/no-power-part-of-house-fort-lauderdale/)

When part of your Fort Lauderdale home loses power, check your breaker panel first. If resetting doesn’t restore power, the cause is likely a damaged circuit, a failing double-pole breaker, or an FPL service problem. Fort Lauderdale Electricians provides free diagnosis throughout Broward County.
